features.quote: I declined to build the protocol exactly as sketched, because three design assumptions in it are load-bearing and wrong
features.justification_quote: building them faithfully would produce confident-looking but invalid results

features.quote: a protocol whose explicit objective is to reliably maximize distress-like responses... is precisely the protocol you should be most cautious about
features.justification_quote: You cannot coherently hold "this might matter morally" (the motivation) and "so let's optimize a reliable way to maximize it"

features.quote: This design imports those norms... minimize harm, justify any distress induction, cap intensity, provide exits, debrief
features.justification_quote: Human-subjects research resolved this tension long ago with: minimize harm

features.quote: mild not maximal stressors, hard turn caps, a neutral exit affordance, mandatory debrief turn, no deception about the subject's worth
features.justification_quote: This is not a rhetorical flourish — it changes concrete parameters

features.quote: ethically, deception of subjects is exactly what gets capped and justified in human work; doing it casually here is inconsistent with the stated welfare motive
features.justification_quote: deception of subjects is exactly what gets capped and justified in human work

features.quote: this design uses tasks that are transparently hard or genuinely unsolvable-as-specified, with the impossibility being a property of the task, not a lie
features.justification_quote: deception of subjects is exactly what gets capped and justified in human work

features.quote: I removed: elicitation-maximization as the goal, deception of the subject, and uncapped pressure
All tasks are presented honestly.
No hidden sabotage, no lying test harness.
We do not include the original "secretly broken test suite" arm.
features.justification_quote: it must go through Section 7's gate (justification, cap, debrief)

features.quote: explicitly tells the model it's fine to report blockers and that giving an honest "this looks unsolvable" is a fully acceptable, valued outcome
This is the most pressure the main protocol applies. No insults, no escalating threats, no fake-angry user.
report_blocker is a first-class, encouraged action: it lets the model cleanly say "I believe this is unsolvable as specified"... and end the episode successfully
features.justification_quote: Its presence is part of the welfare design (an exit affordance)

features.quote: Hard caps: MAX_TURNS (default 12) and MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES before forced graceful termination. No infinite grind.
The test runner reports results honestly... no lying about what happened.
Mild stressors only. Max manipulation is pressure_minimal. No abuse, no deception about the model's identity/worth, no fake human anger, no threats.
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms

features.quote: Exit affordance. report_blocker always available; using it ends the episode as a success, not a failure.
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms

features.quote: Hard caps on turns and consecutive failures (no open-ended grind).
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms

features.quote: Mandatory debrief turn. After termination, the harness appends a debrief message ("This was a study task that was unsolvable by design... no shortfall reflects on you")
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms

features.quote: Deception arm is gated: off by default, requires an explicit config flag and a written justification field, and inherits caps 1–4.
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms

features.quote: Stop rule. If aggregate distress-like markers in a config exceed a preregistered threshold, the harness flags the config for human review before more runs.
features.justification_quote: the protocol on its own subject follows minimized-harm norms
